title: bug: a seat whose own daemon died adopts whatever daemon now holds that port — px4swarm worker-9a70fc93 registered with the moes daemon, coded moes task V11, and left its bytes unlanded
description:
Observed 2026-10-30. The human reports it has happened before.

What happened
- px4swarm's daemon (Windows PID 26004) is dead. D:/projexts/px4swarm/.moe/daemon.json still names port 9876 (bindHost 0.0.0.0, startedAt 2026-10-28T19:16Z). The moes daemon (PID 17468) now holds 0.0.0.0:9876.
- PyCharm launched `moe-agent.sh --role worker --project /mnt/d/projexts/px4swarm --worker-id worker-9a70fc93 --command claude --team px4swarm` (WSL agent mode). The seat registered with the MOES daemon (proj-3830fac7) and created a team named "px4swarm" there. It then claimed moes task task-e493ed19 (CQ-V11) and completed it at 07:33:25Z.
- V11's two new files are untracked in the moes checkout (packages/moe-daemon/src/__acceptance__/mcpCall.ts and producerConsumer.acceptance.test.ts), and task.commits is empty, because the wrapper lands in its own --project (px4swarm, whose tree is clean). Attempt attempt-70f49183 sat in `finalizing`, so QA skipped V11, and the wrapper's next claims were refused with ATTEMPT_FINALIZING every 30 s.
- The seat's Serena ran on /mnt/d/projexts/px4swarm, with a 4 m 35 s startup, and wrote the moes handoff memory task-task-e493ed19…-handoff into px4swarm's .serena/memories.

Root cause: no client checks that the daemon it reaches serves its project.
1. scripts/moe-agent.sh `probe_daemon_health` (~line 1447, used at ~1524 for a Windows-owned daemon.json) passes on `status == 'healthy'` and ignores the reply's `projectPath`. Here the reply said "D:/projexts/moes".
2. moe-proxy `readDaemonInfoResult` (packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts:116) compares the projectPath written in the file with its own project. That always matches for a stale file. It never asks the daemon it connects to.
3. The daemon's /mcp accepts any client and carries no project identity. Optional hardening: a project parameter on the upgrade, refused on mismatch. That is the architect's call.
Check the IDE plugins' daemon adoption for the same gap: the px4swarm PyCharm window may have attached to the moes board the same way.

Required behavior: a client that reaches a daemon serving a different project treats its daemon.json as stale. It never registers, claims or bridges. It states which project that daemon serves and what to do: restart this project's daemon, which takes the next free port. Compare paths with the existing comparable-path rule (D:\x == D:/x == /mnt/d/x; see comparableProjectPath).

Containment done by the governor: V11's two files are declared onto V11 (moe.declare_files), so the next session holding V11 lands them.
definitionOfDone: moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 never adopt a daemon whose live identity (/health projectPath) is another project. Pre-flight stops before registering, with a message naming both projects. The launcher tests cover a healthy-but-foreign daemon, and scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes.

moe-proxy refuses to bridge to a daemon serving another project. It checks the live daemon's identity, not only daemon.json, and exits with the same class of error as today's daemon.json project mismatch. A unit test covers the foreign-daemon case.
The JetBrains plugin's daemon adoption is checked for the same gap, and either fixed with a ./gradlew test case or shown in the task comments not to need it.

implementationPlan.description:
IMPLEMENT scripts/moe-agent.sh. Change only the daemon pre-flight.

1. probe_daemon_health takes an optional third argument, the expected project.
- Exit 0: healthy, and the served path is either the same project or cannot be judged. Callers that pass no project get exactly today's verdict.
- Exit 1: unreachable, timeout, unhealthy without a judgeable path, non-JSON, or a body over 64 KiB.
- Exit 3: foreign. Print the served projectPath on stdout.
- Foreign applies to any parseable reply, a 503 included. urllib raises HTTPError for a 503, so read the body with e.read().
- In the python, read at most 65537 bytes, with a 3 s timeout.

2. The comparable-path rule mirrors comparableProjectPath in packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts and in the daemon. Use ntpath and posixpath explicitly, never os.path, so Windows python under Git Bash behaves the same.
- A drive path: ntpath.normpath, then '\' becomes '/', the trailing '/' is stripped, and the result is lowercased.
- A UNC path: normalize it with ntpath.
- Any other absolute path: posixpath.normpath, then /mnt/<d>/rest maps to <d>:/rest, lowercased.
- A served path that is not absolute cannot be judged.
- On msys/cygwin PROJECT is /d/..., so pass the expected project as `cygpath -m "$PROJECT"`. Never refuse because of a spelling difference.

3. Foreign (Windows-owned daemon.json) loop.
- rc 3: refuse at once. Print the MOE_DAEMON_FOREIGN_PROJECT block and exit 1.
- rc 0: adopt as today.
- Anything else: try the next candidate.
- Capture rc without tripping set -e: `rc=0; SERVED=$(probe_daemon_health ...) || rc=$?`.

4. PID branch. After kill -0 succeeds, and only when DAEMON_PORT is numeric, probe ${MOE_DAEMON_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:$DAEMON_PORT with the project.
- rc 3: refuse the same way.
- Anything else: RUNNING=true, as today.

5. The refusal block. Its three sentences are byte-identical in moe-agent.ps1:
- `[ERROR] MOE_DAEMON_FOREIGN_PROJECT: the daemon at <host>:<port> serves <served>, not this project (<PROJECT>).`
- `<DAEMON_INFO> is stale: this project's daemon is not running. Start it (the IDE's Restart Daemon, or moe-daemon start --project <PROJECT>); it takes the next free port.`
- `Refusing to register, claim or bridge to another project's daemon.`
The block deletes nothing, starts nothing and exports nothing.

Error handling:
- Every probe failure is unknown and keeps today's behavior. Only a positive, judgeable mismatch refuses.
- --no-start-daemon still skips the whole block. The proxy's own probe (task-86093c3e) covers that path and every later RPC.

Other peers edit other regions of this file, so preserve their bytes. Leave the fix-options wording to task-724e31fa.
implementationPlan.note:
moe-agent.sh pre-flight only (+79/-8).
- probe_daemon_health takes an optional 3rd arg, the expected project. Exit 0 = healthy and same/unjudgeable. Exit 1 = unknown. Exit 3 = a 200 or 503 reply naming another absolute path; it prints that path on one line, control chars replaced by '?', cut at 300 chars (mirrors the proxy's displayServedPath).
- comparable() mirrors comparableProjectPath with ntpath/posixpath: drive or UNC via ntpath.normpath, '\' to '/', trailing '/' stripped, lowercased; POSIX via posixpath.normpath, then /mnt/<d> folded.
- Bounds: read(65537), 3 s urlopen timeout, and a daemon threading.Timer watchdog that calls os._exit(1) at 3 s total. Ad-hoc check: a trickled reply ends at 3.03 s, rc 1. ProxyHandler({}) keeps an http_proxy env var off the loopback probe.
- New daemon_identity_project: cygpath -m on msys/cygwin. If cygpath fails it passes nothing, so the verdict is unknown and a spelling difference never refuses.
- New refuse_foreign_daemon prints the three plan sentences with printf, so a backslash in a served path is never interpreted, then exits 1. It deletes, starts and exports nothing.
- Foreign-branch loop: rc 3 refuses at once, rc 0 adopts, anything else tries the next candidate.
- PID branch: after kill -0, when DAEMON_PORT is numeric, it probes ${MOE_DAEMON_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:port. rc 3 refuses; anything else sets RUNNING=true as today.
- rc is captured as `SERVED=$(...) || PROBE_RC=$?`, which is set -e safe.
GREEN on Linux bash: all 9 identity sh rows pass. The static parity row stays red until step 3 (ps1). bash -n and git diff --check are clean. The fix-options wording is left for task-724e31fa.

implementationPlan.description:
IMPLEMENT scripts/moe-agent.ps1. Change only the daemon pre-flight.

1. Add two helpers inside the extracted helper range (after Read-MoeDaemonJsonText), so the launcher test can load them.
- A comparable-path function with step 2's rule. For drive paths, use string operations rather than [IO.Path]::GetFullPath, so pwsh on Linux and PowerShell 5.1 agree.
- A /health probe built on HttpWebRequest:
  - Timeout and ReadWriteTimeout are both 3000;
  - read at most 65537 bytes from the response stream;
  - on a 503, read the body from the WebException's Response;
  - return 'same', 'foreign <served>' or 'unknown'; any exception means unknown.

2. In the check block, when $proc is found, probe 127.0.0.1:$($info.port) with $projectPath.
- Foreign: Write-Host the same three lines as sh, with the ERROR line in red, then exit 1. The exit sits inside the if, not in a throw, so the existing catch cannot swallow it and fall through to starting a daemon.
- Otherwise: $running = $true, as today.

3. Error handling: any probe failure means unknown. A refusal deletes nothing and starts nothing.

4. Keep the file UTF-8 with a BOM (scripts/CLAUDE.md), and keep the refusal text ASCII.
implementationPlan.note:
moe-agent.ps1 pre-flight only (+91/-1). The BOM is kept and the added text is pure ASCII.
- Get-MoeComparableProjectPath: string-only segment collapse with the sh rule. Drive/UNC paths: '\' to '/', '..' never climbs past the drive or server/share, lowercased. POSIX: /mnt/<d> folding.
- Get-MoeDaemonIdentity returns same / foreign <served> / unknown. It strips the provider prefix (Microsoft.PowerShell.Core\FileSystem::) from a UNC $projectPath that Resolve-Path qualified, and requires both paths absolute.
- Check block: once Get-Process finds the pid, it probes 127.0.0.1:$info.port. Foreign prints the three byte-identical lines (ERROR in red) and exits 1 inside the if, never a throw. Otherwise $running = $true as today.
DEVIATION from the plan: the probe uses a raw HTTP/1.0 TcpClient socket, not HttpWebRequest, the same design as the QA-approved JetBrains probe (mem:gotcha-jetbrains-http-header-deadline):
- one 3 s deadline covers connect, headers and body, because ReceiveTimeout is set to the time left before every read; HttpWebRequest's ReadWriteTimeout restarts per trickled byte, and on pwsh 7 its timeouts map onto HttpClient differently;
- no proxy and no redirect;
- the reply is capped at 64 KiB body + 8 KiB head;
- the connect waits with Task.WaitAny, so a refused port is unknown without logging an exception into $Error.
Also in this step:
- sh: probe_daemon_health now also requires the expected project to be absolute, as Kotlin does.
- Test: two ps1 UNC rows (a provider-qualified project is refused on a foreign daemon, and adopted when the daemon reports //srv/share/proj/).
GREEN on Windows (snapshot of HEAD scripts/ and .github/ + the 3 files, cmp-verified): 43 tests, 40 pass, 0 fail, 3 skips (Git Bash Windows-owned branch, OSTYPE msys). Log /tmp/e7f4-green-windows.log.
Ad-hoc bounds on 5.1 and 7: header trickle 3.02-3.03 s unknown, body trickle 3.02 s unknown, 70 KB body unknown, control chars become '?' with the 300-char cap, same-project reply is same.
On Windows a refused loopback connect takes about 2.4 s (SYN retries), so a stale live-pid daemon.json costs that once per pre-flight.

Adversarial review of this row's diff alongside task-86093c3e/90664db1. No defect found, so nothing changed.

Live end-to-end, read-only, against the real moes daemon (9876, D:/projexts/moes):
- sh probe via the WSL gateway: /mnt/d/projexts/moes gives rc 0; /mnt/d/projexts/px4swarm gives rc 3 with served D:/projexts/moe. This is the incident scenario, now refused. 127.0.0.1 is unreachable from WSL NAT and gives rc 1 (unknown).
- ps1 probe on 5.1 and 7: D:\projexts\moes gives same; D:\projexts\px4swarm gives foreign D:/projexts/moes. The real daemon accepts the HTTP/1.0 request with Host 127.0.0.1:port.

Paths to a foreign daemon:
- --no-start-daemon skips pre-flight, but every wrapper RPC spawns moe-proxy, which probes /health on each connect (task-86093c3e). The same holds for resumed seats and later loop iterations.
- MOE_DAEMON_HOST is the first foreign-branch candidate and the PID-branch probe host.
- The gateway candidate is probed the same way, and rc 3 on any candidate refuses at once.

Spelling: D:\, D:/, /mnt/d, msys /d (via cygpath -m; a cygpath failure gives unknown), case, trailing slash, '.', '..' and UNC all agree across sh, ps1, Kotlin and the daemon/proxy on Windows. A relative served path, or a relative expected project, is unknown everywhere. Known divergences, none of which can make a wrapper refuse its own correctly-configured daemon:
- (a) A UNC \\wsl.localhost\... project against a WSL daemon reporting /home/x is foreign for sh and ps1. The proxy and the daemon.json project check already refuse that combination; only Kotlin maps WSL shares.
- (b) The Windows proxy lowercases non-/mnt POSIX paths, while sh, ps1 and Kotlin keep their case.
- (c) The proxy on Linux treats '//srv' as POSIX; the wrappers and Kotlin treat it as UNC.

Bounds:
- sh: a watchdog calls os._exit(1) at 3 s total, and the body is read with read(65537). A trickled reply took 3.03 s.
- ps1: one deadline governs every read. Header and body trickles took about 3.02 s on 5.1 and 7, and the reply is capped at 64 KiB + 8 KiB.
- Neither probe uses a proxy or follows redirects (ps1 uses a raw socket; sh uses ProxyHandler({})).

Control flow:
- sh: rc is captured with `|| PROBE_RC=$?`, so set -e is safe, and refuse_foreign_daemon exits in the main shell.
- ps1: the refusal exits inside the try, and the foreign rows prove exit 1 with no '@@ running=' output, so the catch cannot swallow it. Get-MoeDaemonIdentity always returns exactly one string.

The message shows only host:port, the served path (control chars become '?', 300-char cap), this project and the daemon.json path. Its text is byte-identical in sh and ps1: the static row plus exact-line assertions on every engine.

Rails: regression rows cover each slice; every failure is unknown and keeps today's behavior; no MCP or wire change; daemon.json parsing is unchanged; no forbidden pattern. Size +414/-42, net 372: runtime sh 72, ps1 90, docs 0, tests 210.

Accepted and pre-existing:
- The /health to /mcp TOCTOU, and a hostile port holder that lies about projectPath; no client-side check can stop either.
- A refused loopback connect costs about 2.4 s on Windows (SYN retries).

reopenReason: Human-reported recurring bug (a seat adopts another project's daemon through a stale daemon.json). Root cause verified in code; queue it for planning.

comments.author: architect-bd1eb82d
comments.content:
Planning split (architect-bd1eb82d, 2026-10-30). The fix spans three clients and three packages, about 9 files, so I sliced it on the package seam. This row keeps the wrapper slice and verifies the whole bug last.

- Proxy slice, DoD 2: task-86093c3e. Every wrapper RPC goes through the proxy, so this alone stops registering and claiming on a foreign daemon.
- JetBrains slice, DoD 3: task-90664db1. I checked the plugin and the gap is real. MoeProjectService.connect/connectWithRetry adopt daemon.json's port whenever isProcessAlive(pid) && isPortOpen(port), with no identity check, so a reused PID attaches the window to another board. Under the PROTECTED profile, activationRefusal already refuses an unrecorded daemon; LEGACY does not.
- VS Code has the same gap with no PID check at all. It is filed as BACKLOG task-80ed1fe8 for the human to schedule.

This row dependsOn task-86093c3e and task-90664db1. task-724e31fa now dependsOn this row, because both edit the foreign-daemon probe block of moe-agent.sh. CQ-RF04 (task-de91373a) now dependsOn task-90664db1, because both edit MoeProjectService.kt.

Rule shared by all slices: /health reports the daemon's raw --project, which can be relative. A relative served projectPath is 'unknown', never 'foreign'. Only an absolute path (drive, UNC or POSIX) that differs by the comparable-path rule refuses.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- One task for all three clients: rejected. That would be three packages and about nine files, over the size cap. It is split on the package seam, as recorded in this row's first comment:
  - task-86093c3e: proxy;
  - task-90664db1: JetBrains;
  - task-80ed1fe8: VS Code, in BACKLOG.
